title: Text Analyzer
story: Every letter in English has a personality. 'E' appears ~12.7% of the time — the most common. 'Z' barely shows up at 0.07%. Your program can reveal these hidden patterns in any text — the same technique that cracked the Zodiac killer's ciphers.
why: Character and word frequency analysis teaches counting with Map, sorting by value, and data-driven text insights — the foundation of NLP and cryptography.
analogy: Counting different colored M&Ms in a bowl: red=5, blue=12, green=3, yellow=8. Blue wins. Your text analyzer counts letters and words the same way — 'E' is usually the blue M&M, dominating every English text. Frequency analysis is just counting candy.
try_it: Analyze this sentence for letter frequency: 'the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'. Who wins — E or O? Add word frequency: track each unique word and its count. Print the top 3 most common words. What does this reveal about the text?
tips: Convert char to index: `c as Int - 'a' as Int`
English letter frequency: ETAOIN SHRDLU (most to least common)
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle uppercase — convert to lowercase first
Using a Map when a 26-element Vec is faster for letters
Counting spaces and punctuation as characters
